items.summary: The July 11 morning Hormuz session opens on the first morning following the conclusion of the Khamenei state funeral — a geopolitically structuring event that resolves the analytical ambiguity that defined the July 8-10 MOU Acute Stress period. Ali Khamenei was killed on February 28, 2026 in the joint US-Israeli strike package that opened the war. His state funeral ran from July 3 to July 10, encompassing public mourning periods in Tehran, processions to Qom, ceremonies in the Iraqi holy cities of Najaf and Karbala, and culminating in his burial at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad on July 9-10. The 7-day ceremony represented Iran's largest state funeral in its modern history — upwards of 30 million attendance across the full national mourning period per Iranian state media. The funeral's conclusion is analytically significant for the MOU's near-term trajectory for one reason: mourning protocols imposed a de facto diplomatic pause on Iran's willingness to engage the Doha communication channel agreed July 9-10 between Witkoff/Kushner and Qatari/Pakistani mediators. Iran's refusal to use the channel during the funeral period was not straightforwardly adversarial — it was partially structural. That structural constraint expires this morning. Al Arabiya and Times of Israel both reported in their July 10 evening cycles that US-Iran negotiations are anticipated to resume on July 11, with the nuclear issue explicitly on the agenda. If confirmed, the resumption represents the MOU's re-engagement as an operative framework — the most significant positive development since the June 19 signing — rather than mere survival under acute stress. The MOU's formal termination instruments remain absent through the July 11 morning session: no SNSC formal void declaration, no CENTCOM naval blockade reinstatement order, no Kharg Island strike confirmed. The June 28-29 ballistic missile exchange (Iran striking US facilities in Kuwait and Bahrain; CENTCOM retaliatory strikes) and the July 7-9 second-wave exchange (3 tankers struck; 85+ US facilities targeted; CENTCOM second-wave strikes) are formally unresolved under MOU architecture but have not produced formal MOU termination. The oil sanctions reimposition (July 7 — Iranian crude export waiver revoked) is the central MOU incentive gap still operative; the communication channel agreed July 9-10 is theoretically the mechanism to address this dispute, but has not yet been used for substantive negotiation. WTI pre-market is approximately $71-72 per barrel on July 11 — below the $73-74 'de-risk from peak' band that characterized July 10, and approaching the $69-71 normalization-confidence zone that Lloyd's of London and commercial shipping companies use as a normalization trigger. The directional shift from $75 (July 9 re-escalation peak) to $71-72 over 48 hours reflects Iran supply return partially suppressing the war-risk premium — a more substantive signal than the Qatar channel premium trim that produced the July 10 retreat. The 60-day nuclear window is at Day 23 of 60 — 38% elapsed — with no formal nuclear technical talks yet scheduled. The Iran succession dynamics are the most uncertain medium-term geopolitical variable: the Assembly of Experts will begin its process to designate a new Supreme Leader, and the competing factions (IRGC hardliners, pragmatic clerics, Mojtaba Khamenei candidacy questions) will shape whether the MOU's nuclear architecture accelerates or stalls over the next 37 days.

items.summary: Five secondary geopolitical threads entering the July 11 morning session. First: Russia struck Kyiv overnight with precision weapons targeting military-industrial complex enterprises, per the Russian Defense Ministry. The scale and nature of the July 11 overnight Kyiv strike is consistent with the pattern of large Russian strategic strike packages in the Ukraine theater since early 2026. The July 6 earlier in this session period saw one of 2026's largest Russian packages (351 drones, 68 missiles, 12 killed); the July 11 overnight strike represents continued high-intensity prosecution of the Ukraine campaign concurrent with the Hormuz MOU acute-stress period. The Ukraine theater is not in operational convergence with the Hormuz dynamic today — no NATO Article 5 trigger, no direct US-Russia exchange — but Russia's continued strategic strike tempo at maximum intensity during the MOU acute-stress period is geopolitically relevant context for the broader US-adversary management challenge. Second: Russia fuel crisis Day 11. The CDU-10 + CDU-11 combined 75% offline assessment at the Omsk refinery (Russia's largest, with ~440,000 bpd nameplate capacity) is confirmed at the July 11 morning session. CDU-10 (38% of capacity) is classified as destroyed — multi-month restoration timeline. CDU-11 (37% of capacity) is halted due to supporting infrastructure damage — potentially recoverable sooner. Combined 75% offline renders Omsk functionally non-operational for primary crude distillation. Russian regional fuel disruptions are confirmed in 78 of 83 internationally recognized Russian regions. Diesel export ban is in effect through July. Central Asian knock-on effects: Uzbekistan has cut flights due to jet fuel shortages; Kazakhstan is insurance-sourcing Chinese imports. The IEA has designated the Russia fuel situation 'unprecedented' in post-Soviet context. For the Warsh September SEP scenario: the CDU-10 'destroyed' classification extends the Russia-refining inflationary shock contribution well past the September FOMC horizon, which — combined with the Hormuz corridor's partial throughput — represents a persistent two-source supply-side inflationary challenge to the Warsh data-dependence framework's deflationary impulse thesis. Third: Lebanon fragile hold Day 26. No confirmed operational direction from Iran to Hezbollah following the July 8-9 CENTCOM second-wave exchange and Iran counter-strikes on 85+ US facilities. The ceasefire-war oversight committee (formed June 30) is nominally active. Hezbollah's 'null and void' declaration on the Rubio framework remains formally unretracted. The absence of Iran operational direction through Day 26 is analytically meaningful — the funeral period is one reason; Iran's interest in preserving the MOU communication channel as a pressure instrument may be another. If Iran talk resumption is confirmed on July 11, Lebanon's ceasefire status may stabilize as a byproduct. Fourth: Peru Fujimori JNE credentials ceremony T-4 (July 15, Grand National Theater). Fifth: Colombia de la Espriella inauguration T-27 (August 7). Venezuela earthquake Day 18 — 1,719+ dead, 46,600+ missing, Maduro restricting US humanitarian access.

items.summary: The July 11 morning economic session opens with WTI pre-market at approximately $71-72 per barrel — a level that is analytically distinct from July 10's $73-74 print. The July 10 brief characterized that level as 'de-risking from peak — not normalization confidence.' The $71-72 territory on July 11 represents a different signal: it is at the upper edge of the $69-71 normalization-confidence zone that Lloyd's of London and commercial shipping insurers have historically used as a re-normalization trigger. The price move from $75 (July 9 re-escalation peak) to ~$71-72 in 48 hours is being driven by Iran supply return actively contributing to the market — not simply a war-risk premium retreating passively. The distinction matters: supply return is a durable supply-side signal; premium retreat is a sentiment signal. If Iran supply return is driving the sub-$72 print, it is more robust to geopolitical noise. Against this: the July 7 reimposition of Iranian crude export sanctions — which stripped the MOU's central economic incentive for Iranian participation — remains operative. The communication channel agreed July 9-10 is theoretically the mechanism to address the sanctions dispute; if July 11 talk resumption is confirmed, the sanctions dispute becomes the first substantive agenda item. Without sanctions resolution, the WTI trajectory toward normalization is limited — the market is pricing in a communication-channel confidence premium, not a sanctions-resolved confidence premium. Federal Reserve picture: the June 17 FOMC minutes (released July 8) confirmed a 9-9 split on the dot, with Chair Warsh withholding his own dot — the first Federal Reserve minutes in modern history to show a sitting Chair declining to participate in the Summary of Economic Projections. September hike odds are approximately 50-55% entering the July 11 session. The June Jobs report (57K, significant miss vs. 150K+ consensus) complicates Warsh's implicit hawkish-data-dependence framework — weak labor adds a deflationary impulse that partially offsets the Russia fuel crisis and Hormuz corridor inflationary drivers. The net: the data picture is genuinely ambiguous entering the July 13-17 data week, which includes June CPI, Warsh's first Congressional testimony as Fed Chair, and June PPI. These data releases will substantially narrow the September FOMC outcome probability distribution. Oregon gas: ~$4.68. National average: ~$3.85. Both represent material declines from the June 23 peaks ($5.35 OR / $4.56 national) — post-deal retail relief is delivering. SK Hynix's July 10 Nasdaq debut at $26.51B was the largest-ever foreign company Nasdaq IPO — a market-liquidity and risk-appetite data point indicating institutional confidence persists despite the Hormuz acute-stress period.

items.summary: Four secondary economic threads entering July 11 morning. First: FERC's June 18 Section 206 AI-informational-reporting directive advances to T-7 with July 18 as the hard deadline. All six ISO/RTOs under FERC jurisdiction — PJM, MISO, SPP, CAISO, ISO-NE, NYISO — must file 30-day informational reports on resource adequacy planning for large load interconnection (principally data centers and AI computing clusters). For the Pacific Northwest: BPA is not directly subject to FERC's Section 206 authority, but the FERC-standard methodology that ISO-NE, PJM, and CAISO develop will set the benchmark against which hyperscaler interconnection requests in the BPA territory are evaluated. The July 18 filing deadline's overlap with the Longview CSB elevated-risk window and the measles sub-window closure (July 12) creates a three-thread convergence period that is analytically dense from today through July 18. Second: Section 122 tariff architecture is at T-13 to its July 24 expiry. USTR's Section 301 post-hearing review has a July 20 completion deadline (T-9). No successor tariff framework has been announced. The gap between Section 122 expiry and any Section 301 replacement leaves 12.5% tariffs on 46 countries in an ambiguous legal posture for approximately 4 days (July 24-28). Import-dependent manufacturing and retail inventory decisions are being made now based on assumption of continuity — a legal interpretation that no USTR ruling has confirmed. Third: OBBB (One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed June 30) is at Day 12 effective. The legislation's Medicaid and SNAP provisions are in active state-level implementation in 18 states, with no federal injunction issued. The Aragon v. Rollins June 22 ruling (which invalidated USDA demonstrations in 5 states) creates a downstream conflict with OBBB's SNAP provisions in those states — a legal conflict that has not yet produced a federal court stay. Fourth: the largest affordable housing bill in decades became law on July 10 without President Trump's signature — a passive signature by executive inaction under 10-day constitutional rules. The housing bill is analytically significant as a bipartisan policy product that cleared Congress and became law despite administration ambivalence — a data point on the residual bipartisan institutional capacity of the 119th Congress.

items.summary: The July 11 morning session opens with the Chelan Hills Fire (Douglas County, Washington) at Day 7, with the morning ICS-209 as the session's primary domestic infrastructure verification item. The Day 6 Red Flag Warning context: on July 10, the Chelan Hills Fire — which had surged from zero containment at ignition (July 4, human-caused, likely fireworks near US-97 Orondo) to 20% on Day 4 and 50% on Day 5 with the help of the July 5-8 atmospheric river — faced its first direct weather challenge since the AR period ended. Red flag conditions on July 10 (10-20% relative humidity, wind gusts to 35+ mph in east-of-Cascades terrain with Douglas fir/shrub-steppe fuel mosaic) represented a direct test of the dozer-line geometry that had been established under moderating AR conditions. The overnight July 10-11 read: reports are cautiously positive — no confirmed large fire progression, no Level 3 expansion orders. If the morning ICS-209 confirms 50%+ or better, it validates the containment architecture as robust under red flag conditions and positions the fire for continued containment progress toward full resolution. The fire's human-caused criminal investigation remains active — the Douglas County Sheriff's Office has offered a $25,000 reward. Confirmed metrics: ~9,735-9,861 acres burned, 1 confirmed fatality (human remains recovered July 7, individual refused to evacuate), $9.1M+ structural damage. Sourdough Fire (Day 7): SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) reopened on July 10 — the closure that had isolated the Highway 20 corridor since early July. Skagit dam hydroelectric power restoration is developing. The Sourdough Fire is transitioning to extended-attack posture in roadless Cascade Wilderness terrain — suppression throughput limited by access constraints, but the immediate community and infrastructure crisis (SR-20 corridor access, Skagit power) is stabilizing. North Cayuse Fire (Umatilla Indian Reservation, Oregon): 4,885 acres, 15% contained as of most recent ICS-209. Northwest Incident Management Team 3 took command July 9. 524 personnel and multiple aircraft assigned. Pendleton and adjacent eastern Oregon communities are experiencing moderate-to-unhealthy-for-sensitive-groups air quality from smoke transport. NIFC Preparedness Level 4: Day 13 of the first PL4 since 2021 (elevated July 6 on Sourdough + Chelan Hills concurrent crisis). 38 large fires nationally across 14 states; 541,000+ total acres in those fires. National year-to-date: 3.4 million acres burned through early July, representing 146% of the 10-year average. USFS structural context: the Forest Service has lost nearly 6,000 permanent employees since early 2025, with fuels treatment acreage reduced 35% — the suppression deficit entering the 2026 above-normal fire season is structural, not cyclical.

The convergence is the brief's highest-consequence domestic infrastructure risk-concentration period of the 2026 calendar outside an active incident. Thread 1 (Longview elevated risk window): the Longview, Washington Longview CSB facility's elevated chemical vapor pressure risk window opens July 11-18 — the annual summer period in which temperature-driven vapor pressure dynamics peak in above-average-temperature conditions. Thread 2 (FERC AI report T-7): the July 18 FERC informational reporting deadline, which requires all six ISO/RTOs to file resource adequacy plans for AI/data center large-load interconnection, falls on the last day of the Longview elevated risk window. Thread 3 (measles sub-window): the high-consequence measles incubation sub-window (June 19 Lumen Field exposure; two-day clean streak July 9-10) closes tomorrow, July 12. The three threads don't cause each other; they overlap in time, creating a compressed window in which the brief's primary industrial safety risk (Longview vapor), primary grid regulatory deadline (FERC AI filing), and primary public health monitoring peak (measles sub-window Day 3) all converge. items.summary: Three primary domestic legislative threads on July 11 morning. First: the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBB, signed June 30) advances to Day 12 as active federal law. Medicaid and SNAP provisions are in rollout implementation in 18 states. The legislation's most immediate downstream conflict: the Aragon v. Rollins June 22 ruling by a federal judge invalidating USDA state-level demonstrations in 5 states creates a direct conflict with OBBB's SNAP provisions in those states. No federal court has issued an injunction against OBBB's SNAP changes as of the July 11 morning session. The legal conflict between the June 22 ruling and OBBB's SNAP architecture will need to be resolved in federal district courts in the affected states — a litigation timeline that runs parallel to the administrative implementation. Second: SAVE America Act (Trump's signature voter ID legislation) is advancing through the House reconciliation pathway despite substantial obstacles. Speaker Johnson committed after the House's return to Washington to advance the SAVE America Act through a reconciliation bill. The obstacle: Senate Parliamentarian Elizabeth MacDonough ruled during the prior reconciliation push that the SAVE America Act's provisions do not comply with Senate reconciliation rules (the Byrd Rule). The House can pass the bill under reconciliation processes, but Senate Parliamentarian resistance will create a procedural conflict. Senate Republicans are skeptical that the parliamentarian's ruling can be overridden — but some GOP members have floated the 'nuclear option' on parliamentarian rulings. Third: a bipartisan affordable housing bill became law on July 10 without President Trump's signature — the President took no action within the constitutional 10-day window, allowing the bill to become law passively. Described by NPR as the largest affordable housing bill in decades, the legislation passed with bipartisan support. Its passive signing is analytically significant as a data point on the administration's willingness to accept legislative outcomes it did not actively champion, and on the residual bipartisan legislative capacity of the 119th Congress.

items.summary: The July 11 morning PNW fire brief is anchored by the Chelan Hills Fire's Day 7 overnight red flag test result — the session's single most important domestic infrastructure verification. The Day 6 scenario, analytically: the July 10 Red Flag Warning (10-20% RH, 35mph+ gusts, east Cascades terrain, late-afternoon instability) represented the first direct weather challenge to the 50% dozer-line containment geometry that the 200+ suppression personnel had established during the July 5-9 atmospheric river period. The AR period (July 5-8) enabled the suppression progression from 0%→20%→50% under moderating humidity recovery; the Day 6 conditions reverted to the terrain and weather profile that produced the zero-containment Days 1-3 catastrophe. The containment geometry's robustness under Day 6 conditions was the primary open question of the July 10 session. The overnight July 10-11 read: no confirmed large forward fire movement has been reported through the morning open; no Level 3 evacuation expansion was ordered. These are cautious positive signals, but definitive confirmation awaits the morning ICS-209 filing — expected by mid-morning. The fire's human-caused investigation context remains active: the Douglas County Sheriff's Office is pursuing the ignition-source responsible for the July 4 holiday fire, with a $25,000 reward outstanding. One confirmed fatality (human remains recovered July 7 from burned vehicle; victim refused evacuation). $9.1M+ in documented structural damage, with 100+ structures destroyed or damaged. If the ICS-209 confirms containment holding at 50%+ through the red flag event, it positions the Chelan Hills Fire for continued progression toward full containment and the closure of all remaining evacuation orders. Sourdough Fire (Day 7): the July 10 afternoon's SR-20 reopening is the session's secondary positive confirmation. The North Cascades Highway — closed since the Sourdough Fire's first week — has reopened, restoring the primary corridor through the northern Cascades for recreational, commercial, and emergency traffic. Skagit dam hydropower restoration is developing (power had been cut during peak fire-proximity operations). The Sourdough Fire transitions to extended-attack posture in roadless Cascade Wilderness terrain — a managed-burn approach given access constraints and terrain. No near-term resolution is expected; monitoring continues. North Cayuse Fire (Oregon, Umatilla Indian Reservation): 4,885 acres, 15% contained, NW IMT3 command July 9, 524 personnel. This is the active fire with the most complex jurisdictional terrain — Tribal land, USFS interface, federal agency coordination. Pendleton and adjacent communities are experiencing moderate-to-unhealthy smoke. NIFC PL4 Day 13: 38 large fires nationally across 14 states. First PL4 since 2021 (elevated July 6). National 3.4 million acres burned YTD at 146% of the 10-year average.

analyst_summary: July 11, 2026 morning opens at Vibe 4 — upper edge, firming toward the Vibe 5 threshold that the July 11 session is positioned to reach by afternoon. The morning session's analytical structure is defined by one decisive structural inflection opening and two risk concentrations activating simultaneously. The inflection: the Khamenei state funeral (July 3-10, burial at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad) concluded yesterday, ending the mourning period that imposed a de facto diplomatic pause on Iran's engagement with the Doha communication channel. Al Arabiya and Times of Israel anticipated talk resumption on July 11 post-funeral, with the nuclear issue explicitly on the agenda. If confirmed today, it is the most significant MOU operational positive since the June 19 signing — re-establishing the dispute-resolution architecture as functional rather than merely extant. WTI's pre-market ~$71-72 print supports this reading: the move from $75 (July 9 re-escalation peak) to the upper edge of Lloyd's normalization zone over 48 hours reflects Iran supply return, not merely war-risk-premium sentiment retreat. The risk concentrations: (1) the Chelan Hills Fire's Day 7 morning ICS-209 — confirming whether the July 10 Red Flag Warning's test of the 50% containment geometry held — is the session's primary domestic verification; the overnight read is cautiously positive but unverified. (2) The Longview CSB three-thread convergence opens today (Longview elevated vapor risk + FERC AI T-7 + measles sub-window Day 3), representing the 2026 calendar's highest-concentration PNW risk overlap window. The measles sub-window's two-day clean streak (July 9-10) is the arc's strongest reassurance yet, with the window closing tomorrow July 12. The morning's analytical posture is one of convergence: three directional positives (Iran talk resumption, WTI normalization, Chelan Hills likely holding) are expected to confirm in the same session that the three-thread convergence opens. The evening brief's Vibe 5 is the morning's forecast trajectory, contingent on those confirmations arriving.
